parts:
How would I respond to my nephew after he wrote me this? We are Christian but I am also living on the wild side so I can relate to him. But I want to articulate some thoughts from his loving auntie that is wanting him to respect himself and that he can have both the good girl and the sexy girl. He just needs to raise the bar and love himself enough to know the difference between love and lust. This is what he wrote... Hey man, idk if we should talk about this, or if I should even bring it up... But I've had some intimate feelings/reactions, with some different girls. But I don't understand how to differentiate between "Love" and "Attraction"? Kind of makes me feel like I'm a "whore", derivative of female attention... 

But that being said, how am I supposed to chase the "good girl", as opposed to the sexy one?? 

The "good girl" is BORING. But the "Slut", makes me feel complete. 

Am I just supposed to become celeaate, and pursue my life? Or use my "attractiveness", derivative of gratification? 

Idk if this makes sense. But whatever your response, I appreciate it!!

Here’s a response that holds your Christian grounding, your real life wisdom, and the “wild side auntie” energy he trusts you for. It’s loving, direct, non judgmental, and gives him a framework he can actually *use*.

You can copy and paste this or let me adjust the tone if you want it more soft, more firm, or more humorous.

---

Hey babe, thank you for trusting me with this. Most guys don’t even have the courage to ask these questions, so you’re already ahead of the game. And what you’re feeling doesn’t make you a whore or broken. It makes you human.

Here’s the truth that took me a long time to learn. Attraction is easy. Lust is loud. Love is quiet and steady. Attraction hits your body. Love hits your soul. And both can exist at the same time, but only one can build a real life with you.

You don’t have to choose between the “good girl” and the “sexy girl”. You can have both in one woman. But you only find her when you respect yourself enough to raise your standards. The “slut” type makes you feel complete in the moment because she’s feeding the part of you that wants validation and excitement. There’s nothing wrong with liking excitement. Just don’t confuse the hit of dopamine with something that can hold your heart.

The “boring good girl” isn’t boring. She’s just not triggering the same quick chemical high. But the right woman will challenge you, steady you, excite you, and bring peace all in one. She just won’t show up until you’re choosing from a place of self respect instead of temporary gratification.

You don’t need to be celibate unless that’s something you feel spiritually led to. And you don’t need to run wild for validation either. What you *do* need is to slow down, listen to your gut, and ask yourself one question every time you meet someone:

“Does this girl make me feel more like the man I’m meant to become or just distract me from becoming him?”

If she elevates you, that’s love potential. If she only excites the moment, that’s attraction. Both have their place. Only one creates a future.

And you’re not just “attractive”. You’re valuable. You’re a man with purpose, faith, talent, and depth. You don’t have to settle for either extreme. You get to build something real with a woman who is both good and sexy because you’ve done the inner work to recognize the difference between love and lust.

I’m always here when you want to talk about this stuff. You’re not alone. I love you.
